title: Explicit four-step coefficient transport of Chern arrows
statement: For categories C0,...,C4, functors Fi:Ci→C(i+1), objects Ui,Vi in Ci, and arrows ui:Fi(Ui)→U(i+1) and vi:Fi(Vi)→V(i+1), define F=F0;F1;F2;F3, u=F3(F2(F1(u0);u1);u2);u3, and v=F3(F2(F1(v0);v1);v2);v3. For c:U0→V0 and c_prime:U4→V4, fourStepChernCommutes means F(c);v=u;c_prime. If every ui is invertible, ti:Vi→Ui satisfy Fi(ti);ui=vi;t(i+1), and c;t0=id, fourStepChernDegree proves c_prime;t4=id. This is purely a composition calculation. For the coefficient application use the following supplied inputs: Let l be prime and let Y and P=ProjectiveLine Y be Noetherian schemes with DiagonalTraceLocalizations at l. Fix a finite intermediate l-adic field E, an element pi of its ring of integers generating the maximal ideal, and n:N. Give an l-adic coefficient Diagram zl, an integral coefficient Diagram integral, and ScalarCompatibility toIntegral for integralMap l E [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams, def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-scalars]. Give tq:DiagonalTrace.Result l ULift(Q_l) (P→Y) with tq.model.model=Iso.refl P [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-presentation]. Give CompletedRealizations completedY and completedP and a full-unit CompletedPushSquare q_square from tq.Rc to zl.Rq [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-reference]. Put A=ULift(O_E/(pi^(n+1))), assume A finite and l^(n+1)=0 in A, and assume l^(n+1) invertible on Y. Give a quotient Diagram d and ScalarCompatibility scalar from integral to d, finite realizations eY,eP, a root-normalized QuotientLineRealization lineP at exponent n+1, and a FiniteTracePresentation presentation [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-quotient-line, lem-diagonal-finite-trace-chern-criterion]. Give c:completedUnit(Y)→tq.Rc(completedLine(P)[2]) such that constant-scalar restriction of c followed by tq.sourceMap equals tq.coefficientsS.unitMap followed by tq.LS.R(systemChern), where systemChern is restriction of tq.model.chernAdjoint followed by tq.varying [lem-diagonal-completed-chern-lift]. The record UniformizerChernNormalizationData stores exactly these inputs and their already supplied normalizations [lem-diagonal-completed-chern-lift, def-sfb-diagonal-trace-presentation]. Its ChernNormalized predicate specializes fourStepChernCommutes to the completed realization, integral and quotient scalar extensions, finite realization, their unit maps, their four specified direct-image comparisons, and the finite positive Chern adjunct [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-reference, def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-scalars, lem-diagonal-finite-trace-chern-criterion, sk-lem-geo-p1-cohomology]. It asserts precisely the Chern-arrow equation before any trace is composed; no Chern-arrow comparison or Chern/trace-degree equation is added as a field of the input record. The auxiliary ChernCoefficientDiagram packages the same formal coefficient data with the two coefficient rings, finite ring A, exponent N, annihilation and invertibility assumptions abstract. Its Commutes predicate is the same four-step equation. Its proved traceDegree theorem obtains finite Chern degree from Commutes, the completed Chern/trace identity, and completed trace compatibility, by using the two supplied scalar trace squares and the finite presentation. UniformizerChernNormalizationData.diagram fills every field by the actual integral and quotient data; ChernNormalized is its Commutes predicate.

proof.text: Define fourStepChernCommutes by the displayed composite functor and composite endpoint maps. All composition and functor operations are supplied data; this is a proposition, with no chosen witness.

For fourStepChernDegree, compose the four trace squares using functoriality and associativity. The composite unit map is invertible. After precomposing the desired equation with that unit map, substitute the Chern comparison, the composite trace square, and F(c;t0)=F(id). Cancel the unit map.

Package the given coefficient diagrams, comparisons, identity-model normalization, finite residue instance, completed Chern lift c, and its system normalization hc in a dependent record. Every field is supplied input; no coefficient-transport or trace-degree equation is added.

Specialize the four functors to completed realization, integral extension, quotient extension, and finite realization. Their ui are the actual unit comparisons. Their vi are the completed derived square followed by the completed line endpoint, the two scalar mates followed by their line endpoints, and the finite presentation comparison. Apply fourStepChernCommutes to the supplied c and the finite positive Chern adjunct. This defines ChernNormalized without asserting its truth. Perform the trace calculation first for ChernCoefficientDiagram with abstract coefficient rings: extract the supplied trace squares, use the inverse of the finite presentation comparison for the last square, and apply fourStepChernDegree. The uniformizer diagram is a constructor whose fields are the actual input maps and records. Define ChernNormalized as its Commutes predicate; this expands to precisely the same displayed four-step Chern equation.

def fourStepChernCommutes
    {C₀ C₁ C₂ C₃ C₄ : Type*}
    [Category* C₀] [Category* C₁] [Category* C₂] [Category* C₃] [Category* C₄]
    (F₀ : C₀ ⥤ C₁) (F₁ : C₁ ⥤ C₂) (F₂ : C₂ ⥤ C₃) (F₃ : C₃ ⥤ C₄)
    {U₀ V₀ : C₀} {U₁ V₁ : C₁} {U₂ V₂ : C₂} {U₃ V₃ : C₃} {U₄ V₄ : C₄}
    (u₀ : F₀.obj U₀ ⟶ U₁) (v₀ : F₀.obj V₀ ⟶ V₁)
    (u₁ : F₁.obj U₁ ⟶ U₂) (v₁ : F₁.obj V₁ ⟶ V₂)
    (u₂ : F₂.obj U₂ ⟶ U₃) (v₂ : F₂.obj V₂ ⟶ V₃)
    (u₃ : F₃.obj U₃ ⟶ U₄) (v₃ : F₃.obj V₃ ⟶ V₄)
